cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: What Really Happened?
cards.instruction: Find the truth by comparing details, repeating questions, and testing which parts of the story remain consistent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. For this missing-parcel form: was it a bag or a box? You've said both. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A bag, I think. I carried it by the handles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Describe the handles. Were they attached to fabric or cardboard?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Cardboard. It had a rigid lid, too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why 'bag'? Tell me again what you carried. Was the box inside something?

mechanism: A leads a missing-parcel form but tolerates an unset label and supplies a sketch while testing the physical details behind bag versus box.
confusable: Unlike forcing the first answer to be right, A compares handles and lid then tests nesting; authority reduces pressure to label immediately so B keeps recalling.
comparison: Object classification differs from reconstructing a lost bag journey through a coffee stop.
seedUse: D126-a handles, cardboard lid and possible outer bag; S02-a adjusts the form process around uncertainty.
